brief: Create a CLI tool in Python to save web links with tags and search through bookmarked links.

hidden_requirements.text: The executable entrypoint must be named `bookmarks.py` in the project root.
hidden_requirements.answer: The CLI should be executed as `python3 bookmarks.py <subcommand>`.

hidden_requirements.text: Bookmarks must be stored in a JSON file named `bookmarks.json` in the working directory as an array of objects: `[{"url": str, "title": str, "tags": [str]}]`.
hidden_requirements.answer: Store bookmarks in `bookmarks.json` in the working directory as a JSON array of objects with keys `url`, `title`, and `tags` (a list of strings).

hidden_requirements.text: The CLI must provide an `add` command: `bookmarks.py add --url <url> --title <title> [--tags <t1,t2,...>]`. Tags must be split by comma, stripped of whitespace, lowercased, and deduplicated. Prints `Saved bookmark: <title>` on success.
hidden_requirements.answer: Use `bookmarks.py add --url <url> --title <title> [--tags tag1,tag2]`. Tags are comma-separated, should be trimmed, lowercased, and deduplicated. Print `Saved bookmark: <title>` when saved.

hidden_requirements.text: Validation & duplicate handling: URL must start with `http://` or `https://`. If invalid, print `Error: invalid URL scheme` to stderr and exit with code 1. If a bookmark with the exact same URL already exists, update its title and tags and print `Updated bookmark: <title>` with exit code 0.
hidden_requirements.answer: URLs must begin with http:// or https://. If not, print `Error: invalid URL scheme` to stderr and exit with code 1. If the URL already exists, update its title and tags in place and print `Updated bookmark: <title>`.

hidden_requirements.text: The CLI must provide a `search` command: `bookmarks.py search [--tag <tag>] [--query <text>]`. When both are provided, both must match (AND condition). Tag matches case-insensitively against the tags list. Query performs a case-insensitive substring search across title and url.
hidden_requirements.answer: Search with `bookmarks.py search [--tag <tag>] [--query <text>]`. If both options are passed, both must match. Tag match is exact but case-insensitive; query is a case-insensitive substring match in either title or URL.

hidden_requirements.text: Search results must be sorted alphabetically by title (ascending) and printed one per line as `[<tag1, tag2>] <title> - <url>`. Tags inside the brackets must be sorted alphabetically. If a bookmark has no tags, output `[] <title> - <url>`. If no bookmarks match, print `No bookmarks found.`
hidden_requirements.answer: Format search output sorted by title ascending as `[<tags>] <title> - <url>` where tags are comma+space separated and sorted alphabetically, or `[]` if none. If no matches, print `No bookmarks found.`

hidden_requirements.text: If `bookmarks.json` does not exist when executing `search`, the command must exit with code 0 and output `No bookmarks found.` without creating any file.
hidden_requirements.answer: If `bookmarks.json` doesn't exist yet, `search` should simply print `No bookmarks found.` with exit code 0 and not create the file.

out_of_scope_answer: That is outside the scope of this project.
